769.t: Yard-party combo with a drummer friend and Frog
769.s: He plays piano-led yard parties in his neighbourhood and forms a small combo with a fat boy called Frog who plays a cornet kazoo.
769.q: And he was a boyfriend of mine, he was a drummer with him and I was right around the corner from my house. I don't care, I was between Biemble and Ivoryville.

267.t: Booker T. Washington school band and Joe Jones's big band
267.s: Ford and Melvin Lastie formed a swing band from the Booker T. Washington band, rehearsing at Corpus Christi. He also met Kid Sheik and played an early job with him.
267.q: Yeah. And he and I were in Booker T. Washington's band, and we made up, all of Booker T. Washington's band made up a swing band. We got Hogan, he was dead, a drummer. He didn't have a set of drums. He had to borrow a bass drum from somebody, and he had a snare drum, stands. And I had alto sax and…

286.t: Growing up with Tillman and the first band
286.s: Russ's first band was Tillman's, with boyhood friends from Sixteenth Ward; they fooled with cheap flutes and formed a band together.
286.q: No. Oh, we were. Yeah, we were. We were fooling around with a flute, you know. Yeah? The bomb fifteen cents flute at the dragon stone.

801.t: How Lawrence drew him into the band
801.s: A group of boys, Josiah and Bush Hall among them, took up instruments, and Lawrence, who managed every band he played in, drew Eddie in. They played a first party for nothing.
801.q: I tell you, there was a bunch of boys around the same age. This little boy was coming up, he was a great connoisseur, they called him Bush Hall. Josiah Frazier was just learning drums. Still on his own show. Right. Still on his own show. What's up, about 16 years old. So they all got interested, so…

303.t: Dick Mackey, the Owls and Tony Almerico on the coast
303.s: Dick Mackey's playing and family, his brother Red, and first playing with Tony Almerico at the Biloxi dog track in 1923.
303.ch: Gulf Coast bands and early jobs
303.q: I know him. Would come over and play jobs with us all the way from New Orleans. Well, it only cost you about $1.35 to come from New Orleans to Long Beach or Gulfport on a train. And that was the first time that I ever played with Dick Mackey. I played drums in that band. The first time I ever…

492.t: Manassas band director Matthew Garrett and the school's musicians
492.s: Dee Dee Bridgewater's father directs the Manassas band; Lloyd lists Harold Mabern, Frank Strozier, George Coleman, Hank Crawford and John Gilmore by grade.
492.ch: Booker Little and the Manassas circle
492.q: Her father, Matthew Garrett was our band director. And he’d get a note that comes to the teacher and says, “Oh, Mr. Garrett wants Charles Lloyd over in the band room, can you excuse him?” Cause you know, the band would play for football. They’d do things so they - The teachers, you know, they had…

400.t: The Chicago Defender boys' band under Major N. Clark Smith
400.s: Mrs. Malone's building became the Chicago Defender's, and Smith formed a young band with Lionel Hampton, who tried to keep Hinton out for his short pants.
400.ch: Cotton Club, Zutty and Chicago traditions
400.q: Madame Walker from Indianapolis, Indiana. She‟s got a big building that‟s still there now and she came. So they bought these buildings. They were the ones that had money. They bought these building to put up these… to give these young girls a chance to get some education in cosmetology, hair…

28.t: Starting a band with the Walker brothers and Phineas
28.s: He began studying clarinet and organised a band with the Walker family and his friend Phineas, rehearsing to the delight of the neighbourhood and a bulldog.
28.q: to put on my body and I am a brown-skinned man and I can't understand that but I used a cane about a couple of weeks and after that I forgot about the cane and that was it. Then I began to study the clarinet. I studied the clarinet and there were five buddies I had, they were called the Walker…

566.t: The little school band, her boyfriend Sprat Morton and Bill Beason
566.s: After the tape turns over, she describes how tight the little band was. Her childhood boyfriend was trumpeter Bernise 'Sprat' Morton, who later played with Roy Eldridge in Horace Henderson's band but got no farther than Buffalo; drummer Bill Beason later played with Chick Webb.
566.ch: Central High, first records and leaving home
566.q: He certainly was a very good drummer. He was one of the great ones. I don't know how he got out of the business or why he got out. He was really good.

235.t: Sy Jenkins's high school band and Howard Brockington
235.s: The weekend band began around 1937 under older West Indian-born Sy Jenkins with trumpeter Howard Brockington; Nicholas was included because of his tenor playing and listening to Chu Berry.
235.q: : Yeah. Yeah, Sophomore. Yeah, well, Sy Jenkins, he was a very energetic fellow and the whole family, they liked music. I remember his brother, he played a little trumpet, he didn't keep it up, and the other brother played drums. But Sy--I didn't realize this at the time--Sy he was a West Indian…

30.t: First big band with Gaspard and the 'Tiger Rag' rehearsal
30.s: A neighbour named Gaspard needed a clarinetist, persuaded Bigard's family to let him play, and the first piece at rehearsal was 'Tiger Rag'; Bigard, reading straight four-four, could not get the dance two-four feel.
30.q: And my first big job with a big band was fantastic. That's the one with a fellow named Gaspard and they were looking for a clarinet player. And he used to -- he lived right near my home and he used to hear me every day practicing, so he asked my folks to let me come and play with them on a night…

125.t: Columbia, Missouri: high school parties and the John Dillinger band
125.s: In Columbia, Missouri, he led a high school band called the John Dillinger band, mused about the word jazz, and had given up the violin for piano.
125.ch: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
125.q: And he was not a straightjacket sort of person. He had an appreciation for humor as well as strict ways, you know. But as I said then we lived in places -- I lived in Columbia, Missouri, where I went to high school. And I might even go to that part of my life because this is going into my junior…
